jobs.title: Construction Rigger - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a Construction Rigger to support the buildout of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. In this hands-on role, you will plan and execute lifts, land mechanical equipment, and keep construction moving on our next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with mechanical, structural, electrical, and operations teams to rig, signal, and set loads from construction through turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Plan and execute lifts using mobile and tower cranes (as signal person), forklifts, gantries, tuggers, chain falls, come-alongs, and other hoisting equipment.
  • Inspect, select, and install slings, shackles, spreader bars, below-the-hook devices, and other rigging hardware; confirm working load limits, hitch type, and sling angles before a pick.
  • Keep damaged, unlabeled, or out-of-date gear out of service and maintain an orderly rigging crib and laydown yard.
  • Signal crane and forklift operators and run the lift team communication for the duration of the pick, including exclusion zones.
  • Crib, block, roll, and land pumps, cooling towers, air handlers, skids, pipe racks, modules, and other mechanical gear.
  • Assist with simple lift sketches, load paths, and field changes; flag drawing or lift-plan conflicts before the pick starts.
  • Stage, move, and inventory rigging gear and construction materials; fetch and return tools and keep consumables stocked.
  • Open and close work areas: protection, debris removal, scrap segregation, and end-of-shift reset so the next crew can start immediately.
  • Follow LOTO, PPE, lift-permit, and site rules; do not start a lift without authorization and a clear exclusion zone.
  • Report damaged gear, unsafe conditions, and near misses immediately.
  • Support punch-list work and cleanup through system turnover.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Journey-level construction rigging experience: 3+ years of industrial or commercial construction rigging, completion of a recognized rigger or ironworker apprenticeship, or equivalent military experience.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience signaling cranes and executing lifts with slings, shackles, chain falls, come-alongs, and gantries or tuggers.
  • Willingness to work at heights, outdoors, and on a changing data center construction site.
  • Ability to use hand tools, power tools, and material-handling equipment safely.
  • Strong safety mindset and willingness to follow site procedures, including lift permits and exclusion zones.
  • Willingness to work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical construction windows.
  • Prior experience on data center, industrial, or heavy-civil construction sites.
  • Familiarity with load charts, pick planning, and mechanical equipment sets (pumps, air handlers, cooling towers, skids).
  • NCCCO Rigger certification (Level I or II) or equivalent.
  • Qualified signal person certification.
  • Forklift certification; aerial lift or scissor lift certification a plus.
  • OSHA 10 or equivalent training.
  • Ability to read plans, lift sketches, and equipment arrangement drawings.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI data center construction sites and remain onsite during peak construction phases.
  • Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders, lift and position moderate loads and rigging hardware, stand and walk for a full shift, and wear PPE for extended periods, with or without reasonable accommodation.

jobs.title: Construction Scheduler - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Develop, maintain, and communicate construction schedules that the field, subcontractors, and leadership can actually use. You will build CPM baselines, update them from real progress, flag risk early, and explain schedule impact of changes, delays, and recovery plans. This is not a data-entry role. You need enough means-and-methods knowledge to challenge a sequence that will not work in the field.

Superintendents run the work; project managers own cost and contracts; the scheduler is the person who can tell you what is actually driving the end date, what slips if a trade is late, and whether a recovery plan is real.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build baseline CPM schedules from drawings, specs, estimates, bid packages, and construction sequences (WBS, activity coding, logic, calendars, and constraints used sparingly and correctly).
  • Maintain the live schedule: collect progress from superintendents, project managers, and trades; update percent complete, remaining duration, and logic; publish a clean current-period update on a set cadence (typically weekly look-aheads and monthly official updates).
  • Own the critical path. Identify near-critical work, float erosion, and out-of-sequence progress. Tell the team why the end date moved, not just that it did.
  • Produce three-week (or similar) look-aheads that match the master schedule and what the field can actually crew.
  • Analyze schedule impact of RFIs, change orders, design late-outs, access constraints, long-lead procurement, weather, and labor shortages. Prepare time-impact analyses (TIA) and what-if, recovery, and acceleration scenarios.
  • Coordinate with project managers, superintendents, estimators, procurement, design, owners/CMs, and subcontractors so the schedule reflects committed dates, not wishful ones.
  • Resource-load and, where required, cost-load the schedule. Flag crew stacking, craft shortages, and unrealistic production rates.
  • Prepare narratives, variance reports, S-curves, histograms, and executive summaries for internal reviews and owner/CM submittals.
  • Support claims and delay documentation with contemporaneous records (as-planned vs. as-built, fragnets, delay categorization) when needed.
  • Enforce schedule standards: naming, coding, update process, backup, and version control so the file remains auditable.
  • Facilitate or support pull-planning / Last Planner sessions and convert those commitments into logic in the CPM model.
  • Visit the site regularly. A scheduler who never walks the job will be wrong.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 4+ years of construction scheduling on active projects (GC, CM, owner’s project controls, or specialty contractor).
  • 4+ years of experience using Smartsheet, MS Project, or similar and comfortability with multiple calendars, relationship types, filters, layouts, global vs. project data, and schedule quality checks (open ends, negative float, SS/FF overuse, constraints). 
  • 4+ years of experience with owner/CM specification-driven schedules (e.g., DCMA 14-point, USACE, or similar quality metrics).

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s in construction management, civil engineering, or a related field — or equivalent field experience.
  • PSP (AACE), PMI-SP, PMP, CCM, or similar credential.
  • Experience with owner/CM specification-driven schedules (e.g., DCMA 14-point, USACE, or similar quality metrics).
  • Forensic delay analysis, time-impact analysis, and claims support.
  • Cost/resource loading, earned value, and integration with cost systems.
  • Last Planner / pull planning; BIM 4D (Navisworks, Synchro) is a plus.
  • Additional tools as applicable: Power BI, Smartsheet, Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud. 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willing to work extended hours as needed, including the current 6-day / 12-hour construction cadence.
  • Must be comfortable working in a fully onsite environment. 

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversee and coordinate electrical installations including underground duct banks, conduits, cable pulling, terminations, switchgear, transformers, generators, UPS systems, PDUs, and grounding for SpaceXAI Data Centers.

  • Ensure all contractors adhere to electrical scope, delivering high-integrity power systems critical to data center uptime and operational readiness.
  • Monitor daily progress of electrical construction, maintaining detailed logs, red-line drawings, and as-built documentation for power infrastructure.
  • Develop and enforce aggressive construction schedules while keeping the project on time and within budget.
  • Champion and enforce SpaceXAI's safety program, building a zero-incident culture across all teams working around energized equipment, excavations, and heavy electrical installations.
  • Supervise foremen and electrical crews, fostering teamwork and accountability in a high-stakes mission-critical environment.
  • Proactively resolve on-site challenges — material delays, technical conflicts, sequencing issues, and coordination with other trades — with a strong focus on electrical system reliability and code compliance.
  • Conduct regular site inspections to verify compliance with local regulations, electrical codes, safety protocols, and SpaceXAI's stringent quality standards.
  • Prepare and present clear progress reports, electrical construction metrics, and risk updates to senior leadership.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years managing electrical construction teams with strong emphasis on large-scale industrial or mission-critical electrical projects.
  • 3+ years of direct hands-on experience in electrical installations including underground duct banks, high-voltage/medium-voltage systems, cable pulling/terminations, switchgear, and power distribution — ideally on industrial processes or heavy power projects.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Postsecondary diploma or degree in construction management, electrical engineering, or related field.

jobs.title: Controls Engineer (Power Generation) - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Join the power generation engineering team to design, commission, and maintain plant control systems. As a Controls Engineer, you will own BOP PLC/HMI and the control-room SCADA picture that brings generation and balance-of-plant into one operating view — Solar, 6000, and BOP on a single set of screens. You will work from control philosophy through commissioning and ongoing reliability, hands-on at the panel and in the control room. The position is based in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other sites. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Own BOP PLC and HMI design, programming, and commissioning for power generation balance-of-plant systems (fuel gas, water, compressed/instrument air, HVAC, cooling, electrical auxiliaries, and related process/utility systems) 
  • Design and maintain the plant SCADA architecture so operators have one operating picture in the control room integrating Solar, 6000, and BOP — graphics, alarms, historian, and situational awareness on a single platform 
  • Develop control philosophy, control narratives, I/O lists, network drawings, cause-and-effect diagrams, and HMI/SCADA standards for reuse across the facility 
  • Specify PLC, HMI, SCADA, remote I/O, industrial networking, and interface hardware; define data exchange with OEM turbine/generation controllers (Solar and 6000) and with electrical protection, metering, and plant systems 
  • Program, test, and troubleshoot PLC logic and HMI applications (IEC 61131 — ladder, function block, structured text as applicable) 
  • Integrate OEM packages and third-party systems into plant SCADA using industrial protocols (Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, IEC 61850, and others as required) so Solar, 6000, and BOP operate as one system 
  • Commission controls: I/O checkout, loop checks, functional testing, HMI validation, alarm rationalization, and start-up support; stay hands-on with technicians and operators 
  • Support day-to-day operations: troubleshooting, sequence issues, bad actors, and control changes under MOPs/MOC 
  • Maintain configuration management for PLC/HMI/SCADA programs, as-left files, firmware, and network documentation 
  • Coordinate with electrical, mechanical, fluids, protection, and operations so controls scope is fully integrated through construction, commissioning, and turnover 
  • Apply relevant standards for industrial control systems and electrical work (NFPA 70 / 70E, IEC 61131, and site cybersecurity/ICS practices such as NERC CIP where applicable) 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, controls engineering, computer engineering, or another engineering discipline 
  • 3+ years of experience in PLC, HMI, and/or SCADA engineering (design, programming, or commissioning) on industrial or power generation systems 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

  • 5+ years in a controls role at a power plant, independent power producer, OEM, EPC, or heavy industrial facility 
  • Hands-on BOP PLC/HMI experience on gas turbine or similar generation projects 
  • Experience building a unified control-room SCADA/HMI that aggregates multiple OEM controllers (e.g. Solar, 6000, or equivalent turbine packages) with plant BOP 
  • Familiarity with major platforms (e.g. Ignition, Allen-Bradley/Rockwell, Siemens, Emerson, GE, SEL) and industrial networking (IT/OT) 
  • Experience with IEC 61131 programming and protocols such as Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, and IEC 61850 
  • Experience across the project lifecycle: design, programming, construction support, commissioning, and operations 
  • Experience with alarm management, historian, and control-room graphics that operators actually use 
  • Working knowledge of how BOP controls interface with electrical power systems (switchgear, protection, metering) without owning relay settings 
  • Experience managing OEM and contractor interfaces on multi-discipline power or capital projects 
  • Professional Engineering license, or actively working toward one 
  • Ability to support technicians in the field and to remain effective during outages, start-up, and event investigations 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Willingness to perform hands-on work in the plant and control room, including during outages and commissioning 
  • Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support power generation operations 
  • Must be able to work on-site in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other SpaceX facilities 

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a member of the Supercomputer Physical Infrastructure team, you will provide hands-on support for the integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and maintenance of control systems across our AI training campuses. This role focuses on safe, structured execution of repairs and recoveries that maximize uptime; wiring and building industrial control panels; supporting PLC, HMI, and SCADA systems; and keeping cooling plants, electrical distribution, liquid-cooling loops, and data halls running. You will work closely with Controls Engineers on the same team. This position is based in Memphis, TN, with work across the Memphis / Southaven campus.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support integration and commissioning of vendor and OEM equipment into campus BMS, EPMS, and SCADA systems and plant PLC controls
  • Perform safe controls and electrical work within LOTO, arc-flash, interlock, bypass-control, and restart-verification requirements; identify hazards, verify zero energy, validate safety devices after repair, and escalate unsafe conditions or unauthorized changes
  • Maximize uptime of cooling, electrical, and facility control assets through hands-on troubleshooting, basic repairs, and corrective actions on electromechanical, pneumatic, and control systems
  • Wire, commission, validate, build, and maintain industrial control panels and field devices to NFPA 79 and UL 508A standards; replace like-for-like components (power supplies, relays, fuses, terminal blocks, sensors), restore wiring condition, and create accurate redlines
  • Navigate and diagnose PLCs, HMIs, alarms, permissives, sequences, I/O status, and logic behavior; clear approved alarms, perform basic recovery, capture evidence, and support minor authorized parameter adjustments with documentation
  • Set up, diagnose, replace, and validate sensors, instrumentation, and industrial networks serving chillers, CDUs, pumps, and power distribution; verify signals, alignment, scaling, and network health
  • Support controls for VFDs, pumps, valves, and related equipment; perform documented resets, recovery, and safe dry-cycle checks
  • Provide controls support for process-critical campus systems, including cooling plants, liquid-cooling loops, electrical distribution, and fire / emergency shutdown (ESOP); protect plant stability during recovery
  • Perform structured fault finding, root-cause support, and rapid corrective actions to minimize downtime
  • Collaborate with Controls Engineers, facilities operations, and construction to deliver safe, reliable solutions and continuous improvement
  • Maintain accurate documentation, work tickets, and records

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience with mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, or hydraulic systems in a manufacturing, industrial, or critical-facility environment; OR associate's degree in a technical field (controls technology, mechatronics, automation, or equivalent)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Strong working knowledge of NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), NFPA 70E, NFPA 79, and UL 508A
  • Demonstrated hands-on skill in fault finding, structured troubleshooting, electrical panel work, multimeter use, schematic reading, and problem resolution
  • Ability to read, interpret, and redline electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic schematics and drawings
  • PLC and HMI experience or familiarization with Siemens TIA Portal, Beckhoff TwinCAT, and/or Allen-Bradley RSLogix / Studio 5000; ability to navigate alarms, I/O status, sequences, and basic diagnostics
  • Experience with electrical control panel building and wiring; sensors and instrumentation (temperature, flow, pressure, leak detection, proximity, encoders, IO-Link)
  • Experience with SCADA systems (Ignition preferred), actuators, VFDs, interlocks, and industrial networks
  • Experience in data centers, power generation, semiconductor, or other high-reliability industrial environments
  • Excellent documentation and communication skills; familiarity with CMMS or work-ticket systems
  • Creative problem-solver with a high sense of urgency, able to work independently or as part of a team in a fast-paced environment

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed
  • Must be willing to travel to other locations
  • Ability to work onsite in the Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS area
  • Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted
  • Must be able to walk and stand for long periods of time, and to climb ladders, bend, stoop, and work in tight spaces

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

SpaceXAI’s legal team plays a critical role, working closely with finance, tax, accounting, operations and engineering, to achieve our mission. This role is for someone passionate about working at the intersection of AI and law.

As a Corporate Counsel, you will support and lead mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, partnerships and other strategic transactions. You’ll also handle corporate governance and subsidiary management and provide counsel to multiple internal clients on a wide variety of complex legal and business issues.

This role is full time, five days a week, on-site and based in either Palo Alto, CA, Washington D.C., Austin, TX, or New York, NY.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead and support mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, investments, partnerships and other strategic transactions from start to finish, including diligence, deal structuring, drafting, negotiating, executing and integrating
  • Partner closely with corporate development, finance and operation teams to execute a smooth and efficient deal process
  • Drive post-closing integration
  • Build processes, templates, and playbooks for mergers and acquisitions and strategic transactions 
  • Advise on corporate governance, including subsidiary board matters and consents 
  • Oversee subsidiary maintenance, including formations, dissolutions, and compliance across US and international entities 
  • Provide counsel on general corporate matters
  • Willingness to roll up sleeves and possess a can-do attitude

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • J.D. from an accredited law school
  • 6+ years in Corporate or M&A at a top-tier law firm or in-house company

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Imagine Product team is redefining AI-driven media experiences for Grok users worldwide. In this role, you’ll build the communications system that meets creators where they are: public proof of what Grok Imagine can do, programs that show creators how it makes them faster, more cost-efficient, or more ambitious, and a community that runs from individual makers to production houses. The job is to move the brand from talking about itself to making other people talk about it — through proof, craft, and community. If you’re a hands-on communicator who can turn product capability into credible stories, repeat advocates, and a feedback loop back into the product, this is your opportunity to make a lasting impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own creator and community communications strategy for Grok Imagine — plan and execute outreach that turns product capability into visible proof, creator adoption, and durable brand affinity.
  • Build and ship product-showcase content across owned channels.
  • Design and run influencer programs as two distinct motions: awareness partners who put Grok Imagine in front of volume, and craft partners.
  • Build relationships with production houses, studios, and in-house creative teams. Get Grok Imagine into real editorial and post-production pipelines, and run a two-way channel so professional workflow feedback reaches the product.
  • Manage external production when in-house capacity is not enough — bidding, contracts, workflow, and quality control — in close partnership with creative leads who set the taste bar for anything that ships under Grok’s name.
  • Track how competing AI media products talk to creators and professionals. Build the measurement that shows which communications work actually drives adoption, and that can support investment in the work.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Proven experience leading communications, creator partnerships, or community programs for a consumer or creator-facing product, including shipped showcases, tutorials, case studies, or creator programs that moved people from curiosity to practice.
  • Hands-on operator: you can write a brief, run outreach, ship a content calendar, manage a vendor, and stand up a curation and rights-clearance pipeline without a large team underneath you.
  • Experience working with creators, influencers, or professional media practitioners, and judgment about which voices confer reach versus which confer credibility.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; you can be precise with internal partners and compelling with external audiences.
  • Strong editorial judgment and a clear standard for what can go out under the brand.
  • Comfort operating in a small, high-velocity team alongside product, research, design, and engineering.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Background in AI-driven media, generative tools, or adjacent creative software.
  • Experience running both broad-reach influencer programs and credibility-building partnerships with working professionals.
  • Familiarity with production, post-production, or studio workflows — and how new tools actually enter them.
  • Experience managing agencies or production vendors end to end.
  • Analytics-informed content practice: using performance data to set cadence, format mix, and spend.
  • Demonstrated taste in visual and motion media, and a point of view on what makes generative work look professional rather than novel.
  • Prior work moving a product’s public perception from novelty to working tool.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$140,000 - $196,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at xAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

jobs.title: Critical Facilities Engineer - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Facilities Operations Technician at SpaceXAI, you'll dive in, operating and maintaining the critical facility systems that power our supercomputing data centers. Working hands-on with MEP systems, you’ll tackle maintenance, operations, and repairs, ensuring peak performance and reliability. Expect to troubleshoot complex issues, streamline processes, and collaborate with teams to keep our infrastructure running smoothly, directly supporting SpaceXAI's mission to accelerate human scientific discovery through AI. 

This role includes the following positions, each with increasing responsibility:

  • Facilities Operations Technician: Independently operate and maintain critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in supercomputing data centers, ensuring high reliability and performance through hands-on maintenance, troubleshooting, and process optimization.

  • Sr Facilities Operations Technician: Perform advanced maintenance and troubleshooting of critical data center systems like HVAC, power, and environmental controls, while mentoring junior technicians to ensure operational reliability.

  • Facilities Operations Lead: Oversee the maintenance and optimization of critical data center infrastructure, including power, cooling, and environmental systems, while leading a team of technicians to ensure operational reliability and efficiency.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Responsible for MEP Infrastructure site safety and environmental compliance, ensuring the sites align with all local and regional health and safety requirements.
  • Provide operational expertise for Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) systems at the datacenter facility. The systems and equipment can include pumps, piping, chillers, cooling towers, CRAH units, wiring, lighting systems, generators, motors, water supply, UPS and switchgear, etc.
  • Routinely inspect all areas to ensure performance measures are being maintained and proactively self-report the problems of facilities.
  • Experience with writing and executing MOPs, SOPs, EOPs.
  • Perform daily inspections of critical systems.
  • Identify and maintain spare parts inventory to minimize downtime.
  • Coordinate and supervise scheduled system shutdowns.
  • Develop and implement energy monitoring metrics.
  • Support commissioning efforts by witnessing equipment startup, assisting with functional testing, and monitoring construction progress.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical or Electrical or 2+ years of hands-on operations/facilities work experience in lieu of degree (data center experience preferred).
  • Knowledge of mechanical or electrical engineering principles and systems (both would be a huge plus).
  • Experience and knowledge of all critical systems documentation including Plans, Procedures, and Operations Manuals.
  • Experience and knowledge of Building and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems and Operations.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience with PLC-based control systems and/or with Building Management Systems (Client).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and technical writing skills in English.
  • Physical Requirements:
    • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
    • Ability to utilize hand tools and power tools as needed.
    • Work is often performed in tight quarters, and physical dexterity is necessary to perform job functions.
    • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs. unassisted.
    • Comfortable working at elevated heights (up to 100 feet) with appropriate safety gear.
    • Comfortable working in extreme outdoor environments—heat, cold, rain, etc.
    • Comfortable working in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.
  • Available to work flexible shifts providing 24x7 coverage as needed, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Position is subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing.
  • Position is subject to pre-employment and annual post-employment background checks.
  • Willing to travel as needed (up to 10%).
  • Valid driver’s license.

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As an Data Center Technician, you will be responsible for the health of our server and network infrastructure for Data Centers. ABOUT THE ROLE:

Join the High Power Engineering team supporting SpaceXAI to design, build, operate, and maintain electrical infrastructure for AI training campuses. As a Design Engineer on the Data Center team, you will work with a small on-site team to scale high-capacity power systems on a schedule set by compute demand. The position is based in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Produce and maintain single-line diagrams, three-lines, panel schedules, cable schedules, conduit and raceway layouts, grounding plans, and equipment elevations.
  • Perform load calculations, voltage drop, cable ampacity and derating, conduit fill, and pull-tension analysis including long underground runs.
  • Size MV/LV transformers, switchgear, busway, and feeders; specify impedance, BIL, temperature rise, and short-time ratings.
  • Write equipment specifications and technical bid evaluations for ring-main units, transformers, switchgear, busway, and PDUs.
  • Supply model inputs to protection and power-system studies: nameplate data, impedances, cable constants, and as-designed configurations.
  • Resolve field RFIs and issue design changes during construction.
  • Maintain organized design and asset documentation for Data Center electrical packages.
  • Ensure compliance with NFPA 70, 70B, 70E, NESC, and IEEE standards, prioritizing safety and engineering excellence.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of electrical design experience in data center, industrial, or utility facilities.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience producing issued-for-construction drawing sets in AutoCAD, AutoCAD Electrical, or Revit.
  • Working knowledge of NEC Articles 110, 215, 240, 250, 310, and 450.
  • Medium-voltage cable system design experience.
  • Experience with power systems analysis software and tools: ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, Matlab, PSCAD, etc.
  • Revit or BIM coordination experience.
  • Engineer in Training certification, or on track for a Professional Engineer license.
  • Experience on a repeated, multi-phase build rather than one-off projects.
  • Demonstrated initiative, creative problem-solving, and strong analytical/engineering fundamentals.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.
  • Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support construction, energization, and operations.
  • Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.
  • Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.
  • Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.
  • Willing to work on-site in Memphis, TN. This is not a remote or hybrid role.
  • Travel up to 25% for factory witness testing, vendor and OEM engagement, and supporting other sites.
  • Valid driver's license.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Director, Memphis Power Plant Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the gas turbine power generation facility supporting SpaceXAI's Colossus data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee. This role oversees all plant operations, maintenance, commissioning, and continued construction/expansion of the dedicated power plant, with full ownership of delivering reliable, high-availability electrical power to the Colossus AI training clusters. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence, ensuring 24/7 power reliability and quality, safety, environmental compliance, and leading cross-functional teams to achieve aggressive scale-up, availability, cost, and schedule objectives in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Memphis gas turbine power plant, including 24/7 operations, maintenance, commissioning, and ongoing construction and capacity expansion
  • Own end-to-end delivery of electrical power to the Colossus data center sites, ensuring industry-leading reliability, availability, power quality, and redundancy
  • Lead multidisciplinary teams of operators, maintenance technicians, engineers, contractors, and support staff in a 24/7 operational and construction environment
  • Oversee plant performance, commissioning, testing, and seamless integration with data center electrical infrastructure and load
  • Develop and execute comprehensive operations and maintenance strategies, including preventative/predictive maintenance, outage planning, hot gas path management, and OEM coordination for gas turbines, generators, balance of plant, and high-voltage electrical systems
  • Manage concurrent construction, equipment installation, civil works, and phased capacity expansions while maintaining safe, reliable operation of the existing plant
  • Ensure full compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements, including air permits, emissions controls, TDEC, EPA, OSHA, and local authorities
  • Partner closely with xAI data center operations, engineering, fuel suppliers, OEMs, utilities, and regulatory agencies
  • Formulate and execute operating budgets, fuel management, O&M, capital projects, and annual operating plans
  • Drive continuous improvement in plant availability, heat rate, emissions, cost, safety metrics, and operational processes
  • Establish and promote a culture of uncompromising safety, accountability, operational excellence, rapid execution, and collaboration
  • Serve as the site leader and primary representative to the Memphis community, regulators, and stakeholders
  • Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing talent; manage staffing, resource allocation, and contractor oversight for both operations and construction

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or other engineering discipline
  • 8+ years of experience in power generation operations, plant management, or related industrial or aerospace operations
  • 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams of operators, technicians, and engineers
  • Experience operating or managing gas turbine power plants (simple cycle or combined cycle)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience managing large-scale gas turbine facilities (100 MW+), preferably with high-availability critical power applications (data centers, industrial, or similar)
  • Proven track record of achieving and sustaining high plant availability, reliability, and low forced outage rates
  • Hands-on experience with plant construction, commissioning, start-up, and concurrent operations/expansion of gas turbine facilities
  • Deep knowledge of gas turbine technology (aeroderivative and/or heavy-duty frames), performance optimization, emissions controls (SCR, etc.), and balance of plant systems
  • Experience with high-voltage electrical systems, generators, switchgear, protection, and data center or industrial interconnection
  • Strong understanding of environmental permitting, air quality compliance, and regulatory reporting for combustion turbines
  • Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments requiring simultaneous operations and major construction
  • Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, fuel costs, contractors, and complex stakeholder relationships
  • Excellent oral and written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills
  • Unfazed by major, abrupt changes in strategic direction or aggressive timelines
  • Ability to work in a demanding, autonomously driven, start-up atmosphere

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to support and supervise plant operations and construction outside of normal business hours, including nights, weekends, and on-call response
  • Must be based at the Memphis, TN site
  • Willingness to work extended hours as needed to support plant reliability and construction milestones
  • General physical fitness required; ability to walk the plant site, access equipment, and work in industrial/outdoor environments (heat, noise, etc.)

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

We’re looking for a hands-on operations leader who can build a culture of excellence and accountability, partner tightly across the company, and keep uptime exceptional as we grow.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own Cluster Uptime: Serve as extreme owner of node, rack, and cluster health across 5+ sites running 24/7, accountable for customer Service Level Agreements and consistently exceptional uptime on SpaceXAI's supercompute cluster.
  • Lead a Large Operations Organization: Direct a 250+ person team spanning site managers, shift supervisors, and technicians across four 24/7 shifts, building a culture of excellence and accountability at every layer of the org.
  • Drive Node and Rack Remediation: Ensure systematic recovery of failed nodes and racks through command-line and physical intervention, driving mean time to repair to the feasible minimum.
  • Partner Across Functions: Coordinate with facilities operations to limit downtime from power and cooling faults and proactive maintenance; with network engineering on cluster upgrades; and with tenant representatives on node remediation and planned and unplanned downtime.
  • Own Vendor Execution: Direct vendors through hardware rework and field operations so repairs, replacements, and capacity work happen at the speed the cluster requires.
  • Lead Site Reliability Engineering: Own the SRE organization responsible for proactive cluster health monitoring, reactive fault mitigation at scale, root cause analyses for node, rack, and cluster issues, and site-wide reliability procedures and fault documentation.
  • Run Data-Driven Improvement: Lead continual improvement and efficiency initiatives, using operational data to balance team resources and raise uptime, repair time, and SLA performance across sites.
  • Command Incidents at Scale: Set the standard for incident response during cluster-impacting events, providing clear direction, fast recovery, and tight communication with internal and external partners.
  • Scale Operations: Standardize best practices across sites and grow the organization in step with cluster expansion, keeping operations consistent as SpaceXAI's footprint scales.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 7+ years of experience working in a large scale operations with 5+ years leading people leaders of technical teams OR 10+ years of experience working in a large scale operations with 5+ years leading people leaders of technical teams.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Proven ability to lead large, multi-site, 24/7 operations organizations in fast-paced, high-responsibility settings.
  • Deep expertise in server hardware, cluster reliability, and data center technologies, from deployment through lifecycle management.
  • Experience supporting compute-heavy environments like AI, machine learning, or high-performance computing at scale.

  • Familiarity with tooling and automation (e.g., Jira, Python, Bash) used to monitor cluster health and improve team efficiency.
  • Enthusiasm for SpaceXAI's mission to accelerate human discovery and unravel the universe.
  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic, mission-focused environment with on-call ownership of cluster-impacting events.

  • Willingness to travel frequently to data center locations to support operations across sites.

You will implement and oversee document control processes that ensure accuracy, traceability, version control, and compliance with internal standards and industry regulations. Working closely with engineering, construction, project management, and quality teams, you will play a key role in enabling fast, organized, and error-free execution of SpaceXAI's ambitious infrastructure buildout.

  • Support regulatory compliance by organizing and maintaining all permits, environmental assessments, safety documentation, and records required for power plant and datacenter operations.

  • 3+ years of experience in Document Control, preferably in construction, data centers, manufacturing, or engineering environments
  • Strong knowledge of document management systems and best practices
  • Excellent organizational skills with high attention to detail
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, SharePoint, and common document control platforms

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience with Procore, BIM 360, Autodesk Construction Cloud, or similar tools
  • Background in data center, industrial, or mission-critical facility projects

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a highly skilled Electrical Commissioning Technician to support the buildout and energization of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. In this critical hands-on role, you will perform commissioning, testing, and troubleshooting of electrical systems that power our next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with construction, engineering, and operations teams to ensure safe, reliable, and high-quality electrical systems from initial installation through full system turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Execute electrical commissioning activities for medium and low voltage power distribution systems, switchgear, transformers, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, and associated controls in data center environments.
  • Perform point-to-point wiring checks, functional testing, calibration, and system integration verification.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve electrical issues during pre-commissioning, commissioning, and startup phases.
  • Develop and execute detailed commissioning test procedures, scripts, and documentation in accordance with project specifications and industry standards.
  • Collaborate with EPC contractors, OEM vendors, and SpaceXAI engineers to coordinate energization sequences and integrated system testing.
  • Ensure strict adherence to safety protocols, LOTO procedures, and quality standards during all commissioning activities.
  • Maintain accurate as-built documentation, test records, and commissioning reports.
  • Support training of operations and maintenance teams on commissioned electrical systems.
  • Participate in constructability reviews and provide field feedback to improve design and installation quality.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years of hands-on electrical commissioning or field technician experience in data centers, power plants, or large industrial facilities.
  • Strong working knowledge of electrical systems up to 480V (medium voltage experience preferred), including switchgear, motor control centers, variable frequency drives, and protective relaying.
  • Experience with commissioning test equipment (meggers, multimeters, relay test sets, power quality analyzers, etc.).
  • Familiarity with relevant codes and standards (NEC, NFPA 70E, IEEE, NETA).
  • Demonstrated ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, schematics, and one-line diagrams.
  • Strong safety mindset with current OSHA 10/30 or equivalent training.
  • Willingness to work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical commissioning windows.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Prior commissioning experience on hyperscale data center projects or mission-critical facilities.
  • NETA certification (Level II or higher) or equivalent (e.g., NICET, Journeyman Electrician license).
  • Experience with data center power infrastructure including redundant UPS, generators, and busway systems.
  • Knowledge of PLC/controls troubleshooting and SCADA systems.
  • Proficiency with commissioning management software (e.g., CxPro, Procore, or similar).
  • Technical degree or trade school certification in Electrical Engineering Technology or related field.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite during peak commissioning phases.
  • Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders, lift moderate loads, and wear PPE for extended periods.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a member of the facility operations team, you will design, build, and activate some of the world’s most technically advanced facilities and data centers. You will be able to operate with autonomy to solve diverse and complex problems, excel at managing multiple projects simultaneously, and work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. You will work with other MEP engineers, trade partners, and internal customers to support these goals and have the opportunity to drive real global impact, ultimately leading to making life multiplanetary. 

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Work in a team environment with other engineering disciplines to provide detailed electrical design and specification for the installation of the following equipment and systems:
    • Electrical power distribution systems.
    • Switch-gear and motor control centers.
    • Exterior and interior lighting.
    • Ground support system controls and ladder logic.
    • Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units.
    • Standby and emergency generators.
    • Automatic transfer switches.
    • Power monitoring hardware and software.
    • Data/phone distribution and wiring.
    • Building and site grounding systems.
    • Fire alarm systems and lightning protection systems.
  • Provide electrical engineering support to facility technicians to troubleshoot existing electrical equipment and controllers.
  • Provide engineering support for the design, operation, and troubleshooting of all the facility's electrical components and systems, including:
    • Load flow analysis of electrical power distribution systems.
    • Electrical equipment evaluation.
    • Building and facility equipment grounding.
    • Power monitoring hardware and software.
  • Ensure that all equipment interfaces properly with other mechanical and electrical systems, including compatibility with facility power budgets.
  • Coordinate all electrical installations and maintenance activities with local electrical utilities personnel.
  • Ensure all electrical designs and installations conform to applicable codes and regulations.
  • Provide code review and analysis utilizing NFPA 70E, NFPA 70 NEC, NFPA 497, NFPA 101, Vol 5 & 6 AFSPCMAN 91-710, and IBC.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of professional experience working on electrical projects, power distribution systems, switchgear, UPS's, and/or generators.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of years of professional experience in a similar role.
  • Professional Engineering (PE) license.
  • Ability to read and understand power and control schematics.
  • Ability to read and understand highly technical equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals.
  • Experience with variable frequency drives (VFDs) and industrial pumps.
  • Experience with controls in MODBUS communication.
  • Experience with medium voltage distribution.
  • Experience with control panel design and production.
  • Working knowledge of power coordination and arc flash.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Power Generation team is seeking an Electrical Technician to operate and maintain plant electrical systems at SpaceX’s power generation facility. You will work hands-on across medium-voltage generation, distribution, and balance-of-plant electrical equipment up to 13.5 kV and 34.8 kV. This is an operations and maintenance role — you will switch, troubleshoot, repair, and keep electrical systems online in a high-reliability, fast-paced plant environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform operations and maintenance on plant electrical systems, including generators, transformers, switchgear, motor control centers, motors, VFDs, UPS units, automatic transfer switches, and emergency/black-start equipment, at voltages up to 13.5 kV and 34.8 kV.
  • Execute switching, isolation, LOTO, racking of breakers, and restoration of medium-voltage equipment in accordance with plant procedures and NFPA 70E.
  • Troubleshoot electrical faults on power distribution, protection, grounding, lighting, and auxiliary systems using one-line diagrams, schematics, and electrical test equipment.
  • Perform preventive and predictive maintenance, inspections, and repairs to improve reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.
  • Support plant startups, shutdowns, outages, and commissioning activities alongside operators, controls technicians, and engineers.
  • Install, terminate, and maintain plant electrical equipment, cable, and control wiring as required for operations and maintenance work.
  • Respond to electrical alarms, trips, and equipment failures; support root-cause investigations and implement corrective actions.
  • Coordinate with operations, engineering, and utility personnel on switching, clearances, and electrical work that affects plant generation.
  • Maintain accurate work orders, switching records, and as-found/as-left documentation.
  • Follow all safety, LOTO, arc-flash, and PPE requirements while working in energized and hazardous plant environments.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 3+ years of experience as an electrical technician, industrial electrician, or similar role maintaining industrial or power generation electrical systems.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience operating and maintaining medium-voltage electrical systems (4.16 kV to 34.8 kV), including switchgear, transformers, and breakers.
  • Experience in a power plant, generating station, or other high-reliability industrial facility.
  • Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, electrical schematics, and equipment O&M manuals.
  • Experience with LOTO, switching procedures, and NFPA 70E / arc-flash safety practices.
  • Experience troubleshooting motors, VFDs, MCCs, UPS systems, and plant auxiliary electrical equipment.
  • Familiarity with electrical test equipment (multimeters, insulation testers, infrared, and similar).
  • Journeyman electrician license or equivalent formal electrical training.
  • Experience using a CMMS or work-order system to plan and close maintenance work.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-discipline operations and maintenance team.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.
  • Ability to work extended hours, nights, weekends, and rotating or on-call schedules to support plant operations.
  • Ability to remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.
  • Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.
  • Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.
  • Must be able to work on-site at the power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceX sites.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Construction Electrician, you will install and terminate new electrical infrastructure: conduit, cable tray, underground duct bank, cable, wire, and 480 V building and feeder work. This is a build job, not an operating-plant job — pull, land, and energize new equipment from drawings, then turn it over. You will follow lockout/tagout and grounding procedures and support first energization of new 480 V systems. This position is based in Southaven, MS.

This is an hourly position with overtime. Expect 80% or more travel on a rotation, with per diem.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Install, terminate, and land new campus electrical equipment, including breakers, transformers, switches, buswork, control systems, and batteries at 480 V.
  • Install conduit, cable tray, cable, wire, and terminations per issued-for-construction drawings; perform underground duct bank, trench, and cable-pull work.
  • Perform installation quality checks and electrical testing (voltmeters, ohmmeters, ammeters, insulation megger) and assist with acceptance and commissioning tests on new gear.
  • Read and interpret construction drawings, one-lines, schematics, wiring diagrams, and work orders.
  • Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), grounding, clearance procedures, NFPA 70E, and PPE requirements on an active construction site.
  • Uncrate, set, and dress equipment; climb structures; operate hand and power tools, pulls, blowers, pumps, and portable generators.
  • Support construction energization sequences, punch-list closeout, and turnover to operations with engineers and vendors.
  • Document work performed, test results, and as-built markups.
  • Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Perform similar or less skilled incidental duties as assigned.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.
  • Current state journeyman electrician license (Tennessee or Mississippi preferred, or equivalent state journeyman license with the ability to obtain TN or MS).
  • 5+ years of industrial or data center electrical construction installing conduit, tray, duct bank, cable, and 480 V terminations.
  • Ability to read construction drawings, one-lines, manuals, and work packages.
  • Proficiency with common electrical test tools (multimeter, megger, ammeter) and construction hand and power tools.
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 70E and lockout/tagout (LOTO).
  • Ability to lift 50+ lbs, work at heights and in confined spaces, and work outdoors in all weather.
  • Hourly position with overtime; willingness to work nights, weekends, and extended shifts during construction and energization.
  • Ability and willingness to travel 80% or more on a construction rotation; per diem and/or housing provided while on site.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Tennessee or Mississippi journeyman electrician license.
  • Industrial, manufacturing, or data center construction experience building raceway and cable plant.

  • OSHA 30 or equivalent construction safety training in addition to NFPA 70E.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As an Operations Electrician, you will keep in-service substations, distribution, and campus power facilities running. This is an operating-plant job: inspect, maintain, switch, and restore equipment so load stays up. You will work with energized medium- and high-voltage systems under established safety standards, perform switching and operations up to 161 kV, and respond to faults and call-outs. This position is based in Memphis, TN.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Operate, inspect, maintain, and repair in-service substation and campus electrical equipment, including breakers, transformers, switches, relays, buswork, control systems, and station batteries.
  • Perform medium-voltage switching and operations up to 161 kV: write or follow switching orders, isolate and de-energize equipment, apply grounds, verify zero energy, and restore equipment to service.
  • Own routine maintenance on medium- and high-voltage operating systems: inspections, lubrication, oil levels, heaters, lights, and connections.
  • Respond to outages, faults, alarms, and call-outs; restore service and document what happened.
  • Conduct electrical testing on in-service equipment (voltmeters, ohmmeters, ammeters, insulation megger) and assist with relay, transformer, and circuit breaker tests.
  • Read and interpret one-lines, schematics, wiring diagrams, and switching orders.
  • Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, and control issues on running plant.
  • Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), grounding, clearance procedures, and PPE requirements.
  • Coordinate switching and clearances with operators, engineers, and utility crews during planned and emergency outages.
  • Document work performed, test results, and observations; keep operating records current.
  • Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Perform similar or less skilled incidental duties as assigned.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.
  • 3+ years of experience working as a licensed electrician.
  • Medium-voltage electrical experience, including switching and operations.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Associate degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial maintenance technology.
  • Journeyman or master electrician license.
  • Switching and operations experience on systems up to 161 kV (substation, industrial, or utility).
  • Experience with medium-voltage switchgear, transformers, and distribution in substations, industrial plants, or data centers.
  • Basic understanding of electrical principles (AC/DC circuits, safety standards).
  • Ability to read prints/drawings and use common test tools.
  • Proficiency with hand/power tools and physical tasks (lifting 50+ lbs, working at heights/confined spaces, outdoors in all weather).
  • Strong safety focus, attention to detail, and ability to work independently or in teams.
  • Knowledge of print reading for drawings, manuals, and one-lines.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; frequent overtime and weekend support is required.
  • Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions, climbing, lifting up to 50 lbs., and working on ladders/lifts at elevated heights.
  • Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, noise, heat, cold, and rain.
  • Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.
  • Stand: up to 6 hours per day.
  • Sit: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Push/Pull: up to 75 lbs. (unassisted) 1–2 hours per day.
  • Overhead reach: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Walk: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Lift/Carry: up to 50 lbs. (unassisted) 1–2 hours per day.
  • Climb (ladder/stairs): up to 3 hours per day.
  • Kneel/Crouch: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Upper body twist: up to 6 hours per day.
  • Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees up to 3 hours per day.
  • Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights, in confined spaces, and working with medium- and high-voltage equipment. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical.
  • Willing to work on-site in Memphis, TN. This is not a remote or hybrid role.
  • Valid driver's license.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As Commercial Counsel at SpaceXAI, you'll provide legal support for some of the world’s largest and most interesting physical infrastructure transactions and development projects. You will tackle complex agreements, bring creative ideas and solutions to key business initiatives and streamline processes in a ludicrously fast-paced environment.  Expect to dive into strategic negotiations, balance legal, business and engineering priorities, and support SpaceXAI mission to advance AI-driven human scientific discovery. This job will have global impact and can be based in Palo Alto, California; Memphis, Tennessee; Seattle, Washington; or Austin, Texas.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead negotiation and structuring of development deals, real estate transactions, capital equipment purchases, hardware and raw material procurement, and much more.
  • Negotiate and manage power-related contracts: interconnection agreements, electricity service agreements, solar project deployments, sustainable storage system transactions, power purchase agreements (PPAs), behind-the-meter generation structures, gas supply / transport, water rights, and ERCOT/regulatory matters critical to hyperscale data center deployments.
  • Draft, review, and negotiate construction contracts, engineering services for design-build, and related project documents for facilities involving insane amounts of power, absurd cooling systems, and advanced cabling and fiber get-ups, all in support of the world’s largest integrated GPU clusters.
  • Support financing structures, tax incentives, complex lease arrangements, permitting activities, easement and land use transactions, and project finance elements that enable multi-billion-dollar-scale infrastructure investments.
  • Partner closely with engineering, security, procurement, business development, and finance teams to align legal terms with technical and commercial requirements.
  • Coordinate effectively with specialized outside counsel on complex matters while maintaining in-house strategic oversight and risk judgment.
  • Contribute to broader initiatives as our data center footprint grows.
  • Be extremely versatile, highly responsive, ability to roll your sleeves up and pitch in for anything and everything needed, even if it’s unfamiliar or not in your lane.
  • Sense of humor, humility, and team-based mentality is a must.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 5+ years of legal experience–ideally through a combination of experience at innovative technology or development companies, and/or excellent law firms.
  • Deep experience in commercial contracting, with a focus on large scale infrastructure projects.
  • Proven track record of effectively managing a heavy workload and ability to prioritize to close transactions according to aggressive business timelines 
  • Tech-savvy with an understanding or interest in datacenters, power, and emerging AI technologies
  • Have a strong sense of ownership and accountability, be inquisitive and enthusiastic about technology, enjoy being continually challenged, and can demonstrate sound judgment in high-stakes and ambiguous situations.
  • Have a lot of charge in the battery!
  • Creative, solution-oriented problem solver.
  • JD from an accredited law school and active bar membership in at least one U.S. state.
  • Commitment to being in-office 5 days/week

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$200,000 - $230,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at xAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Working closely with Sales, Business Development, Finance and Product teams, you’ll tackle complex agreements, analyze and mitigate risks, ensure compliance, and streamline processes in a fast-paced environment. ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Executive Chef plays a vital role in the company, contributing directly to SpaceXAI’s success and historical milestones by overseeing teams within multiple outlets, fueling the workforce overall, and with a particular emphasis on the higher-end food experiences for the company’s guests and/or VIPs. This individual works with the executive staff to conceptualize and oversee multiple outlets and services, ensure consistency across all offerings, and coordinate out-of-this-world employee engagement activities. This position requires a versatile set of restaurant industry skills, an imagination without bounds, and a lot of “can-do” attitude.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Follow, set, and enforce standards of operation in multiple kitchen outlet environments and service formats
  • Support executive chef and/or sous chef/s with operation, team development, and overall department in its entirety
  • Enforce both food and general workplace safety in all food services areas
  • Train staff on work planning materials, safety protocols, and health inspection guidelines
  • Oversee hiring and disciplinary decisions for their team, keeping in mind overall wellbeing of all food services
  • Coordinate successful openings of new outlets, with particular emphasis on VIP experiences
  • Continue operation of new outlets throughout the entirety of there existence once in regular day-to-day operation
  • Plan and meet cost per head targets at their site and/or outlets set by executive chef
  • Support hiring, development, retention and overall team management for all food service’s staff

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • Culinary degree and 4+ years of industry experience; or 6+ years of industry experience
  • 2+ years of experience in a multi-outlet operation facility

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Culinary degree
  • Proficiency in use of Microsoft Office and Outlook software
  • Experience in a corporate environment
  • Experience with high volume or batch cooking
  • Experience leading a group of 20 or more team members
  • Advanced knowledge of kitchen equipment and safe kitchen operations
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Kitchen and or dining area renovation/construction experience
  • Ability to carry large heavy items, such as dishes in tubs or trays unassisted (up to 25 lbs.)
  • Must have or be able to obtain a ServSafe/equivalent state-recognized manager level food handler certification
  • Able to stand for long periods of time – up to 10 hours a day
  • Able to perform frequent bending, stooping, and lifting of objects
  • Must be able to work all shifts and available for overtime, weekends and holiday(s) as needed
  • Must participate in internal leadership and development training
  • Must be willing to travel occasionally
  • Valid Drivers License
  • Valid Food Managers Certification

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Starting base salary is $120,000 USD.

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

jobs.title: Expert Team Lead, Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

You will lead a team of AI Tutors (full-time employees and contractors) responsible for delivering high-quality training data and evaluations that power SpaceXAI’s models. You will set the standard for data quality on your projects, review work in the domain, ensure the accuracy and consistency of the data produced, and build operational excellence at the team level. This is a hands-on leadership role — you will both execute labeling/review work and continuously improve processes as we scale.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own end-to-end quality and delivery for assigned Human Data projects — personally reviewing work in the domain, ensuring accuracy, consistency, guideline adherence, and high-quality data production at scale.
  • Lead, coach, and performance-manage a team of AI Tutors, including conducting regular performance reviews, maintaining records, creating action plans, managing shadow sessions, and driving continuous improvement.
  • Oversee and actively participate in labeling and reviewing tasks to maintain high standards and model best practices.
  • Ensure strict guideline adherence, taxonomy management, and quality assurance processes.
  • Drive efficiency by identifying and resolving operational bottlenecks, implementing process improvements, and tracking performance via KPI dashboards (e.g., quality metrics, throughput, send-back rates).
  • Build, update, and deliver training materials, practice tasks, and certification benchmark tasks; manage certifications and workforce adjustments.
  • Collaborate closely with Human Data Managers, fellow Team Leads, and Engineering to translate model needs into clear labeling strategies and requirements.
  • Coach and develop talent while maintaining strong accountability and a high-performance culture; support disciplinary actions as needed.
  • Document outcomes, suggest process iterations, and report project status, risks, and results.
  • Act as the voice of your tutors while fostering strong collaboration across the broader Human Data organization.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Civil, Environmental, or a closely related engineering field.
  • 2+ Professional experience in engineering practice, such as design, analysis, testing, R&D, or systems integration OR a Master’s degree (or higher) in an engineering or engineering related field.
  • Basic understanding of AI and machine learning concepts and how high-quality training data impacts model performance.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in an engineering discipline, or professional licensure (PE, or FE/EIT).
  • Demonstrated experience with data quality metrics, annotation processes, and guideline-driven workflows (as evidenced by prior roles or projects).
  • Breadth across multiple engineering disciplines, with the ability to credibly review work outside your primary specialty.
  • Experience with performance management, coaching, training program development, and certification frameworks.
  • 1+ years of hands-on experience in data labeling, annotation, AI training/evaluation, content quality, or similar operational domains.
  • Professional experience building scalable, high-performance technology applications.
  • Previous experience leading small teams in data labeling, annotation, or related operations.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong track record of reviewing domain work, ensuring data quality, and improving operational processes.
  • Proficiency in data analysis and associated tools (SQL a plus); ability to use metrics and KPIs to drive continuous improvement.
  • Experience managing mixed employment types (full-time employees and contractors) or distributed teams.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build rapport quickly and align stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational skills, high attention to detail, proactive problem-solving mindset, and focus on continuous improvement.
  • Strategic thinking combined with strong hands-on execution.
  • Specialty or strong domain expertise in at least one of the following areas: Finance, STEM, Coding/Software Engineering, or other technical fields.
  • Passion for building high-performing teams and scaling high-quality Human Data operations.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Candidates must be based in one of the following countries where SpaceXAI has a physical office; remote work is also possible
    - United States
    - Dubai
    - Ireland
    - United Kingdom
    - Ireland
    - Japan
    - India
    - Indonesia
    - South Korea
    - Philippines
    - Singapore

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

US based candidates: $104,000 - $170,400 USD depending on factors including relevant experience, skills, education, geographic location, and qualifications. International candidates: Information will be provided to you during the recruitment process.

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks. Benefits vary based on employment type, location and jurisdiction. Benefits for eligible U.S. based positions include health insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid sick leave. Specific details and role specific information will be provided to you during the interview process.

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.
