jobs.title: Iron Worker (Construction) - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a skilled Iron Worker to support the buildout of SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers and AI supercomputing campuses. In this hands-on role, you will erect structural steel, miscellaneous metals, and equipment supports that form the backbone of our next-generation supercomputer halls, cooling plants, substations, and site infrastructure.

You will work closely with civil, mechanical, electrical, and operations teams to install the steel that carries buildings, pipe racks, cable tray, busway, cooling equipment, and access systems from foundations through turnover. This is a full-time, onsite role with significant travel to SpaceXAI data center sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Erect structural steel for supercomputer halls, mechanical plants, substations, cooling yards, and site buildings, including columns, beams, bracing, joists, and metal deck.
  • Install miscellaneous metals: stairs, ladders, platforms, catwalks, grating, handrail, embeds, and equipment frames that support construction, operations, and maintenance access.
  • Fabricate and install pipe racks, aerial galleries, mezzanines, and support steel for chilled-water piping, cable tray, busway, and liquid-cooling distribution serving AI compute halls.
  • Rig, hoist, and set structural members and heavy equipment-support steel using cranes, come-alongs, chain falls, and approved lifting gear; act as rigger or signal person when qualified.
  • Bolt, torque, weld, and plumb connections to drawings, AISC and AWS standards, and inspection requirements; install high-strength bolts and close connection punch lists.
  • Read structural drawings, erection plans, and shop drawings; lay out from control, check elevations and plumb, and report conflicts before steel goes up.
  • Coordinate with civil, mechanical, and electrical crews so embeds, penetrations, and support steel land correctly for cooling towers, generators, transformers, pumps, CDUs, and IT equipment.
  • Follow fall protection, crane, rigging, hot-work, LOTO, PPE, and permit rules; keep a safe work area at height and around live construction and energized yards.
  • Support inspection, punch-list, and turnover work through building and yard completion.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years of ironworking experience on commercial, industrial, or heavy-civil structural steel, or equivalent military structural or rigging experience.
  • Ability to read structural and erection drawings and work to AISC connection details.
  • Hands-on proficiency with structural bolt-up, cutting, and safe use of aerial lifts, ladders, and material-handling equipment.
  • Willingness to work at heights, outdoors, and on a changing construction site.
  • Strong safety mindset with current OSHA 10 or equivalent training.
  • Willingness to work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical construction windows.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Journey-level ironworker experience (union or non-union) and/or completion of an ironworker apprenticeship.
  • AWS D1.1 structural welding certification.
  • Qualified rigger and/or signal person; NCCCO or equivalent crane, rigger, or signal certification.
  • OSHA 30 and/or fall-protection competent person.
  • Prior experience on hyperscale data center, power plant, industrial, or other mission-critical steel.
  • Experience with pipe rack, equipment support steel, and miscellaneous metals in addition to building steel.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite during peak construction phases.
  • Capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders and structural steel, lift moderate to heavy loads, stand and walk for a full shift, and wear PPE for extended periods.
  • Ability to work at elevation in varying weather, around cranes and heavy equipment, and in active construction yards.

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Our IT Services team is the backbone of our operational efficiency, ensuring seamless connectivity and technical assistance for all our employees, regardless of their location. We are seeking a skilled and helpful IT specialist to join our IT services team. This role provides advanced technical guidance and service to end-users, resolves complex IT issues, and collaborates with Level 1 technicians and senior IT staff to ensure seamless technology operations. The ideal candidate is a problem-solver with strong technical expertise, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to delivering outstanding customer service. This is a full-time position, onsite with occasional on-call or after-hours support. 

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide second-line technical assistance for hardware, software, and network issues via phone, email, or in-person.
  • Diagnose and resolve complex technical problems, including system crashes, network connectivity issues, and software conflicts.
  • Manage and administer user accounts, permissions, and access controls in systems like Active Directory.
  • Assist with the deployment, configuration, and maintenance of hardware (desktops, laptops, servers, and peripherals) and software applications.
  • Monitor and maintain IT systems, including performing patch management, updates, and basic server administration.
  • Document and update IT service tickets with detailed resolutions and escalate unresolved issues to Level 3 experts or specialized teams.
  • Contribute to and maintain IT knowledge base articles and self-service wikis to enhance user self-sufficiency.
  • Support IT projects, such as system upgrades, migrations, or new technology rollouts.
  • Train and mentor Level 1 technicians, providing guidance on troubleshooting techniques and best practices.
  • Ensure compliance with company IT policies, security standards, and data protection protocols.
  • Provide new hire onboarding and offboarding service support

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
  • 2-4 years of experience in IT, helpdesk, or a related technical role.
  • Strong knowledge of Windows and macOS operating systems, Microsoft Office Suite, and common enterprise software.
  • Proficiency in troubleshooting network issues (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPNs) and basic server administration (Windows Server, Linux basics).
  • Experience with IT service management tools (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira) and ticketing systems.
  • Familiarity with virtualization technologies (e.g., VMware, Hyper-V) and cloud services (e.g., Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) is a plus.
  • Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and customer service skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Relevant certifications (e.g., CompTIA A+, Network+, Microsoft Certified Professional, or ITIL) preferred.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience with scripting (e.g., PowerShell, Bash,Python) for automation tasks.
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices and tools (e.g., antivirus, endpoint protection).
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines under pressure.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$68,400 - $102,600 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The IT Systems Team at 𝕏 manages a dynamic and evolving virtual infrastructure that provides secure, high-performance, and reliable corporate resources for business-critical users and applications. This role focuses on building, deploying, and managing on-premises Microsoft Windows Server infrastructure, including Active Directory, VMware Horizon Windows VDIs, and Windows VMs running SQL Server, while collaborating with other teams to deliver scalable, reliable solutions.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build, manage, and support complex application stacks on Windows Server
  • Administer on-premises Active Directory (domain controllers, Group Policy, identity, and access)
  • Deploy, configure, and support VMware vSphere technologies, including vCenter and ESXi
  • Deploy, configure, and support VMware Horizon Windows VDI environments
  • Manage Windows VMs hosting Microsoft SQL Server, including patching, performance, and availability
  • Provide Windows Server troubleshooting and hands-on technical support
  • Manage and support scalable storage solutions, preferably NetApp, in support of Windows workloads
  • Automate Windows infrastructure using PowerShell and related Microsoft tooling
  • Work with engineering teams and third-party vendors to implement scalable solutions
  • Ensure compliance by collaborating with internal audit and compliance teams
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures
  • Participate in a 24/7 on-call support rotation
  • Install, configure, test, and maintain Windows operating systems and system management tools
  • Proactively ensure high levels of system availability and reliability
  • Monitor and optimize Windows application and infrastructure performance, identify bottlenecks, and partner with developers on fixes
  • Write and maintain scripts to improve system efficiency and automation

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are hiring Journeyman Electricians to join SpaceXAI’s internal construction team supporting the rapid build-out of our data centers. This is a traveling role — you will mobilize with project teams to active construction sites, install and commission 480 V electrical systems, and move with the work as new facilities come online.

You will work on 480 V power distribution, busway, PDUs, UPS, main switchboards, grounding, lighting, and process power. This is a construction and commissioning role: pull, land, and turn over new 480 V equipment from issued-for-construction drawings. It is not a facilities-maintenance or operating-plant role.

This is an hourly position with overtime. Expect 80% or more travel on a rotation, with per diem.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Travel with internal construction and electrical teams to project sites to install, terminate, and test 480 V electrical systems, including switchboards, busway, PDUs, UPS, panelboards, generators, conduit, cable tray, feeders, and grounding.
  • Install, terminate, torque, and dress 480 V distribution equipment and associated feeders.
  • Install grounding, bonding, and equipment grounding electrode systems per drawings and the NEC.
  • Support commissioning activities, including point-to-point checks, functional testing, megger testing, and first energization of 480 V systems.
  • Read and interpret electrical drawings, schematics, one-line diagrams, and specifications; produce as-builts and test records.
  • Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA 70E, and SpaceXAI safety and quality standards, including lockout/tagout (LOTO) and arc-flash protocols.
  • Collaborate with contractors, engineers, and operations teams to deliver projects on time with zero incidents.
  • Participate in constructability reviews and provide field feedback to improve designs.
  • Mobilize quickly between project locations as construction phases and priorities shift.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Current state journeyman electrician license (Tennessee or Mississippi preferred, or equivalent state journeyman license with the ability to obtain TN or MS).
  • 5+ years of industrial or data center electrical construction installing 480 V gear (switchboards, busway, PDUs, UPS, main switchboards).
  • Demonstrated 480 V installation, termination, and torque of gear.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, one-lines, and schematics.
  • Proficiency with electrical test equipment (multimeter, megger, torque wrench).
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 70E and lockout/tagout (LOTO).
  • Ability to lift 50+ lbs, climb ladders, and work in industrial environments with PPE.
  • Hourly position with overtime; willingness to work nights, weekends, and extended shifts during construction and energization.
  • Ability and willingness to travel 80% or more on a construction rotation; per diem and/or housing provided while on site.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Tennessee or Mississippi journeyman electrician license.
  • Experience with data center or hyperscale 480 V power infrastructure (redundant UPS, generators, busway systems).
  • Prior work on large-scale, multi-site construction projects that required frequent travel.
  • Master electrician license.
  • OSHA 30 or equivalent construction safety training in addition to NFPA 70E.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Schedule varies depending on site operational needs; frequent overtime and weekend support is required.
  • Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions, climbing, lifting up to 50 lbs., and working on ladders/lifts at elevated heights.
  • Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, noise, heat, cold, and rain.
  • Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.
  • Stand: up to 6 hours per day.
  • Sit: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Push/Pull: up to 75 lbs. (unassisted) 1–2 hours per day.
  • Overhead reach: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Walk: up to 3 hours per day.
  • Lift/Carry: up to 50 lbs. (unassisted) 1–2 hours per day.

You will be able to operate with autonomy to solve diverse and complex problems, excel at managing multiple projects simultaneously, and work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.     • Exterior and interior lighting.
    • Ground support system controls and ladder logic.
    • Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units.
    • Standby and emergency generators.
    • Automatic transfer switches.
    • Power monitoring hardware and software.

  • Ensure all electrical designs and installations conform to applicable codes and regulations.

jobs.title: Lead Engineer, Battery Storage - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Join the High Power Engineering team supporting SpaceXAI to design, build, operate, and maintain electrical infrastructure for AI training campuses. As a Lead Engineer for Battery Storage, you will work with a small on-site team to scale high-capacity power systems on a schedule set by compute demand. The position is based in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own the storage fleet as a power plant, not as an accessory: architecture, sizing, controls, safety case, and grid-forming behavior that lets the campus ride through compute step loads and generation contingencies.
  • Own BESS architecture: pack-to-MV-transformer grouping, string composition, medium-voltage collection topology, string-level protection, and physical block layout including spacing per NFPA 855.
  • Own sizing; translate compute duty cycles — step loads, training-job ramps, actual-versus-nameplate utilization — into power and energy requirements.
  • Own inverter control strategy: grid-forming versus grid-following, droop and virtual inertia, fault-current contribution, ride-through, and coordination with generation governors and excitation.
  • Own the plant controller and EMS functional specification: dispatch, state-of-charge management, peak shaving, spinning-reserve emulation, islanding, and black-start participation.
  • Own the fire and life-safety case: UL 9540 and 9540A basis, thermal runaway propagation, deflagration venting, water supply, emergency response plan, and AHJ engagement.
  • Own the OEM relationship: technical requirements, factory testing, performance guarantees, and degradation and augmentation planning.
  • Direct Design, Commissioning, Ops/Build, Network, Civil, and Program Manager seats on Battery Storage as those seats fill.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.
  • 8+ years in power systems engineering.
  • 4+ years directly on utility-scale or large commercial and industrial battery energy storage.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:

  • Experience sizing storage against a real duty cycle rather than a rule of thumb.
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 855, UL 9540 and 9540A, IEEE 1547, and IEEE 2800.
  • Utility-scale BESS fleet experience at large pack counts.
  • Deep understanding of grid-forming inverter control and its interaction with synchronous machines.
  • PSCAD or other EMT modeling of inverter-based resources.
  • Professional Engineering license or intention to actively seek a PE license.
  • Experience building and leading an engineering team from the first hire.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.
  • Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support construction, energization, and operations.
  • Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.
  • Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.
  • Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.
  • Willing to work on-site in Memphis, TN. This is not a remote or hybrid role.
  • Travel up to 25% for factory witness testing, vendor and OEM engagement, and supporting other sites.
  • Valid driver's license.

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a leading member of the power generation engineering team, you will design, build, and activate technically advanced power plants and generation infrastructure. As a lead engineer, you will lead a team designing, building, and maintaining electrical power systems that directly contribute to new power generation projects. You will be able to operate with autonomy to solve diverse and complex problems, excel at managing multiple projects simultaneously, and work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. You will work with electrical, mechanical, controls, and other engineering disciplines, trade partners, and internal customers to support these goals. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Lead a team of engineers and work in a team environment with other engineering disciplines to provide detailed electrical design and specifications for the installation of the following equipment and systems: 
    • Electrical power distribution systems for power generation plants. 
    • Switchgear and motor control centers. 
    • Plant and yard lighting. 
    • Power plant control systems and ladder logic. 
    • Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units. 
    • Standby, emergency, and black-start generators. 
    • Automatic transfer switches. 
    • Power monitoring hardware and software. 
    • Plant communications, control network, and wiring. 
    • Plant and equipment grounding systems. 
    • Fire alarm systems and lightning protection systems. 
  • Provide electrical engineering support to power plant technicians and operators to troubleshoot existing electrical equipment and controllers. 
  • Provide engineering support for the design, operation, and troubleshooting of all power plant electrical components and systems, including: 
    • Load flow analysis of electrical power distribution systems. 
    • Electrical equipment evaluation. 
    • Plant and equipment grounding. 
    • Power monitoring hardware and software. 
  • Ensure that all equipment interfaces properly with other mechanical and electrical systems, including compatibility with plant power budgets. 
  • Coordinate all electrical installations and maintenance activities with local electrical utilities personnel. 
  • Ensure all electrical designs and installations conform to applicable codes and regulations. 
  • Provide code review and analysis utilizing NFPA 70E, NFPA 70 NEC, NFPA 497, NFPA 101, NESC, IEEE, and IBC. 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or other engineering discipline. 
  • 3+ years of professional experience working on electrical projects, power distribution systems, switchgear, UPS's, and/or generators. 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

  • 3+ years of management experience. 
  • 5+ years of professional experience in a similar role. 
  • Professional Engineering (PE) license. 
  • Experience with power plant or power generation electrical systems. 
  • Ability to read and understand power and control schematics. 
  • Ability to read and understand highly technical equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals. 
  • Experience with variable frequency drives (VFDs) and industrial pumps. 
  • Experience with controls in MODBUS communication. 
  • Experience with medium voltage distribution. 
  • Experience with control panel design and production. 
  • Working knowledge of power coordination and arc flash. 
  • Ability to work on multiple tasks concurrently. 
  • High level of self-motivation, with the ability to work under minimal supervision. 
  • Good organizational skills. 
  • Ability to prioritize and schedule workload. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Join the High Power Engineering team supporting SpaceXAI to design, build, operate, and maintain electrical infrastructure for AI training campuses. As a Lead Engineer for Transmission & Distribution, you will work with a small on-site team to scale high-capacity power systems on a schedule set by compute demand. The position is based in Memphis, TN, with potential travel to other sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own everything from generation terminals and the point of interconnection down to the medium-voltage bus: high-voltage switchyards, collector transmission, main power transformers, and the utility relationship that determines whether the campus energizes on schedule.
  • Own high-voltage switchyard architecture: bus configuration, GIS versus AIS tradeoffs, bus sectionalizing, and fault-current management.
  • Lead the interconnection process with the local distributor and balancing authority, including application, system impact and facilities studies, protection philosophy alignment, telemetry and metering, and technical exhibits to the service agreement.
  • Own campus protection philosophy and the settings management database served to Data Center and Battery Storage — one owner, not three models.
  • Own the campus power systems studies function: the single model of record for load flow, short circuit, coordination, arc flash, and stability.
  • Own the generation electrical interface: excitation and governor behavior, synchronizing, generator protection, black start, and station service.
  • Own regulatory and compliance scope as assigned: service agreements, applicable NERC/SERC standards, air-permitting coordination, AHJ relationships, and compliance evidence.
  • Own the campus electrical safety program: NFPA 70E, arc-flash study currency and labeling, energized work permitting, qualified-worker training, and switching authorization.
  • Direct Design, Ops/Build, Protection & Controls, and Power System Engineer seats on the T&D team as those seats fill.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or another engineering discipline.
  • 10+ years in transmission, substation, or generation interconnection engineering, with a focus on high-power, high-voltage systems.
  • Experience carrying a project through utility or ISO interconnection to energization.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:

  • Professional Engineering license or intention to actively seek a PE license.
  • Working knowledge of the IEEE C37 series, IEEE 80, NESC, and applicable NERC standards.
  • 161 kV, 230 kV, or 345 kV GIS or AIS experience.
  • Large-load interconnection experience with TVA, MLGW, or comparable municipal or federal power arrangements.
  • Experience with power systems analysis software and tools: ETAP, SKM, PSS/E, PSCAD, ASPEN, Matlab, etc.
  • Experience leading a multidisciplinary engineering team.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, work independently, and thrive in dynamic, high-stress environments with tight deadlines.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.
  • Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support construction, energization, and operations.
  • Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.
  • Lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.
  • Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies.
  • Willing to work on-site in Memphis, TN. This is not a remote or hybrid role.
  • Travel up to 25% for factory witness testing, vendor and OEM engagement, and supporting other sites.
  • Valid driver's license.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Lead Fiber Technician on SpaceXAI's traveling data center build team, you will lead crews in the installation, testing, and commissioning of high-performance fiber optic infrastructure across multiple new and expanding data center sites. You’ll bring strong leadership, technical expertise, and a safety-first mindset to fast-paced hyperscale construction projects. This role involves significant travel to support greenfield and expansion builds, ensuring reliable, high-speed network connectivity that powers SpaceXAI's AI training clusters. You will mentor technicians, drive execution excellence, and help deliver mission-critical infrastructure on aggressive timelines.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Serve as crew leader for traveling fiber teams, managing daily work assignments, resource allocation, and execution based on Fiber Span sheets, site surveys, path planning, and cross-functional coordination.
  • Lead and mentor a team of Fiber Technicians across multiple project sites, providing on-the-job training, technical guidance, and performance feedback.
  • Oversee all phases of fiber optic installation projects from planning and mobilization through execution, testing, handover, and closeout at new data center builds.
  • Ensure a safe, productive, high-quality, and compliant work environment in dynamic construction settings.
  • Develop and monitor sensor indicators; conduct timely inspections and quality checks to prevent system issues.
  • Troubleshoot, resolve, repair, and install complex fiber optics systems in both OSP and ISP environments.
  • Lead fiber splicing (fusion and mechanical), termination, labeling, and certification activities.
  • Examine, replace, and optimize faulty or aging fiber optic cables and infrastructure.
  • Organize scheduled maintenance, testing routines, and documentation during build phases.
  • Monitor signal strength, attenuation, and overall network performance; maintain detailed system records, as-built drawings, and designs.
  • Coordinate closely with superintendents, project managers, other trades (electrical, mechanical, controls), and GC teams to align with overall data center construction schedules.
  • Support site mobilization/demobilization, tool/equipment management, and knowledge transfer between projects.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 5+ years of direct experience in fiber optic installation, splicing, and testing in large-scale data center or critical infrastructure environments (Tier 3/4 or hyperscale preferred).
  • 2+ years in a foreman, crew lead, or supervisory role leading fiber/cabling teams.
  • Proven experience working on traveling or multi-site construction/build projects.
  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.
  • Strong hands-on knowledge of fiber optic best practices, OTDR/power meter testing, structured cabling, and safety protocols.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Certification in fiber optics and/or cable installation (e.g., FOA, BICSI, or equivalent).
  • Extensive experience with fusion splicing, high-density fiber deployments, and hyperscale/AI/HPC data center environments.
  • Technical knowledge of communication networks, different fiber types (single-mode, multi-mode, etc.), and associated systems.
  • Background in data center greenfield construction or rapid deployment projects.
  • Experience coordinating with general contractors and multi-trade teams in fast-paced builds.
  • Proficiency with project documentation, digital tools, and quality assurance processes.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively (typically 50-75% or more, depending on project needs) to SpaceXAI data center construction sites across the US, with potential for extended stays at project locations.
  • Ability to work in tight quarters, at elevated heights (up to 50 feet with proper safety gear), and in active construction environments.
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs unassisted and maintain physical dexterity for installation tasks.
  • Comfortable working in high-noise environments and varying weather conditions.
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours as dictated by project schedules and deadlines.
  • Valid driver’s license and clean driving record (company vehicle or travel support provided).

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Lead, Inventory Specialist at SpaceXAI, you will oversee warehouse and inventory operations supporting our rapidly expanding data centers. You will lead the receiving, storage, kitting, issuance, and tracking of high-value servers, networking equipment, power and cooling components, spare parts, and infrastructure materials. In this role you will mentor team members, manage daily priorities and backlogs, drive inventory accuracy, and ensure material is available when needed for construction, commissioning, and ongoing operations. You are expected to be hands-on, maintain a high sense of urgency, and continuously improve processes in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support daily/weekly team meetings by participating in ways to help the team improve
  • Oversee daily shift backlogs and inventory-related queues. Maintain continual oversight of incoming receipts, RMA backlogs, and outgoing material requests to ensure compliance with metric targets
  • Re-assign daily shift resources to meet demands and prioritize critical data center hardware, spare parts, and infrastructure materials
  • Provide input to employees’ performance
  • Function as focal point for area group production coordinators, Site Operations, and priorities related to inventory and material flow
  • Participate in adding to the area’s to-do lists for improvement projects
  • Fulfill resource gaps when shifts are short-handed
  • Mentor employees to meet supervisor expectations for the job
  • Train continuously to improve the workers’ skills in inventory accuracy, material handling, and system processes
  • Monitor department consumables, spare parts, and critical inventory levels; drive reordering and replenishment
  • Monitor the general inventory/fulfillment email inbox and resolve issues promptly
  • Receive, inspect, store, and issue servers, networking gear, power/cooling components, parts, details, and hardware as required to support data center construction, expansion, and operations
  • Store parts and materials in bins, drawers, racks, and designated locations; accurately identify part numbers and storage locations
  • Perform picking functions to make up necessary kits of parts, material, and hardware; ascertain that all items are available and accounted for in kit
  • Maintain strict material handling practices in accordance with procedures, especially for high-value and sensitive equipment
  • Monitor shelf-life storage and maintain proper rotation of stock (FIFO)
  • Maintain accurate environmental and temperature requirements for any temperature-sensitive materials
  • Interface with other fulfillment centers, other sites, Shipping, Receiving, Planning, Quality Control, Purchasing, Procurement, and related departments to resolve problems relative to receipt and distribution of material
  • Maintain good housekeeping and organization of warehouse and staging areas for efficiency (5S principles)
  • Support the organization’s metric goals and objectives for inventory accuracy, cycle count compliance, and material availability
  • Conduct and oversee regular inventory audits, cycle counts, and reconciliations
  • Manage Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) processes, including inspection, documentation, and coordination with vendors

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 2+ years of experience in a warehouse environment
  • 2+ years of experience working in materials management or inventory control
  • Experience with data entry and inventory tracking systems

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Capability to operate a forklift and other related inventory/material handling equipment
  • Experience within data center, technology, aerospace, semiconductor, or high-volume manufacturing environments
  • Excellent computer skills including Microsoft Office / Google Workspace (Word, Excel/Sheets, Outlook)
  • ERP or WMS system experience (SAP, Oracle, or similar)
  • Experience and understanding of inventory, kitting, and RMA processes
  • Detail oriented, organized, and demonstrates a high sense of urgency
  • Prior lead or supervisory experience in warehouse/inventory operations
  • Familiarity with structured cabling, server/hardware handling, or data center material flow

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to lift 25–50 lbs. unassisted
  • Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position
  • Willingness to work flexible shifts, overtime, and weekends as needed to support data center operations and build schedules
  • Must be able to work in a warehouse and data center environment

jobs.title: Lead Technician (Power Generation) - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Lead Technician on SpaceXAI's power generation team, you will lead the technician crew for on-site generation that powers high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Southaven / Memphis area. You will work across plant, process, and electrical systems — gas turbine packages, balance-of-plant, fuel gas and fluid systems, and medium-voltage electrical through 34.5 kV.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform and lead operations, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair across plant mechanical, process/fluid, and electrical systems, including gas turbines and generators, balance-of-plant equipment, fuel gas, water, compressed/instrument air, HVAC and cooling, and plant electrical systems up to 13.5 kV / 34.5 kV
  • Serve as the working technical lead on assigned jobs, shifts, and outages: sequence work, coordinate across disciplines, and keep execution aligned with the supervisor’s priorities and live plant conditions
  • Mentor plant, process, and electrical technicians through on-the-job training, technical guidance, and quality checks — without owning hiring, performance reviews, or formal people management
  • Execute and support switching, isolation, LOTO, start-up, shutdown, racking of breakers, and restoration so mechanical, process, and electrical work is coordinated and safe
  • Troubleshoot complex, cross-discipline plant issues using P&IDs, single-line diagrams, schematics, and test equipment; support root-cause investigations and implement corrective actions
  • Perform preventive and predictive maintenance, inspections, and repairs to improve reliability and reduce unplanned downtime
  • Respond to alarms, trips, and equipment failures; take first action and escalate to the supervisor and engineering as required
  • Support plant start-ups, shutdowns, commissioning, and outages alongside operators, technicians, engineers, and contractors
  • Install, maintain, and restore plant mechanical, process, and electrical equipment as required for operations and maintenance work
  • Maintain accurate work orders, as-found/as-left records, and close-out in the CMMS; uphold procedure and documentation standards
  • Know and enforce safety requirements including LOTO, NFPA 70E / arc-flash, confined space, hot work, and PPE; stop work when conditions are unsafe
  • Coordinate with the supervisor, engineering, operations, and utility personnel on clearances, switching, and work that affects generation

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 5+ years of experience as a plant technician, process technician, electrical technician, industrial mechanic/electrician, or similar role maintaining power generation or high-reliability industrial systems
  • Experience providing technical direction, on-the-job training, or crew-lead support to other technicians

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Hands-on experience in more than one of: gas turbine / plant mechanical systems; process or fluid systems (fuel gas, water, compressed air); and medium-voltage electrical operations and maintenance (4.16 kV to 34.5 kV)
  • Experience in a power plant, generating station, or other high-reliability industrial facility
  • Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, single-line diagrams, electrical schematics, and equipment O&M manuals
  • Experience with LOTO, switching procedures, and NFPA 70E / arc-flash safety practices
  • Experience troubleshooting motors, VFDs, MCCs, pumps, valves, rotating equipment, and plant auxiliary systems
  • Familiarity with electrical and mechanical test equipment (multimeters, insulation testers, infrared, vibration, and similar)
  • Journeyman electrician or millwright license, or equivalent formal trade training
  • Experience using a CMMS or work-order system to plan and close maintenance work
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-discipline operations and maintenance team
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights
  • Ability to work extended hours, nights, weekends, and rotating or on-call schedules to support plant operations
  • Ability to remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE
  • Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted
  • Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position
  • Must be able to work on-site at the power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceXAI sites
  • Valid driver’s license

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

You will lead and develop a team of Facilities Operations Supervisors and Technicians, driving hands-on technical excellence, strategic operational planning, process optimization, vendor management, and cross-functional collaboration. This role emphasizes building a high-performance, team-first culture while ensuring maximum uptime, safety, and efficiency across the site.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Facilities Operations Supervisors and Technicians, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Own the overall maintenance, monitoring, troubleshooting, and performance of data center infrastructure, including HVAC, power distribution, UPS, generators, and environmental systems.
  • Develop, implement, and continuously optimize preventive and predictive maintenance programs, equipment calibration strategies, and system performance KPIs.
  • Create, refine, and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs), emergency response plans, and change management processes to drive operational consistency and excellence.
  • Ensure full compliance with safety regulations, industry standards, and internal policies; champion a strong safety culture across the facilities team.
  • Partner closely with engineering, procurement, construction, and operations teams to streamline equipment intake, installation, commissioning, and lifecycle management.
  • Oversee inventory, asset management, and spare parts strategy using internal applications, ensuring accurate tracking, forecasting, and cost control.

jobs.title: Manager, Engineering (Power Generation & Utilities) - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for a Manager of Engineering to own the design, build-out, commissioning, and continuous improvement of automation, controls, and electrical systems at SpaceX’s power generation facility in Southaven. This plant is critical infrastructure for SpaceX’s AI supercomputers: it must deliver high-reliability power and supporting utilities at scale, with the uptime and response expected of a mission-critical compute campus. 

If it has a gas or steam turbine control system, a switchgear lineup, a plant electrical distribution network, a SCADA/DCS point, a control loop, or a supporting utility/process system (water, wastewater, fuel gas, HVAC, cooling) that must run reliably, this team designs it, specifies it, commissions it, and keeps it running. As a Manager, you will lead a team of engineers in a high-reliability, fast-paced environment. This is a hands-on technical leadership role — you will review P&IDs, challenge control philosophies, dive into DCS/PLC architecture, electrical protection schemes, and commissioning details, not just manage a roadmap. You will scale both the team and the systems as generation capacity and AI compute load grow. 

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

  • Own automation, controls, and electrical scope for power generation assets (gas turbine simple cycle, combined cycle, and steam turbine systems) and plant electrical systems, including DCS/SCADA architecture, PLC systems, turbine control interfaces, switchgear, protection and metering, plant distribution, instrumentation, and control networks — from control philosophy through commissioning and reliability, in compliance with NFPA 70/70B/70E, NESC, and IEEE standards. 
  • Lead controls scope for mechanical and electrical balance-of-plant and supporting utilities, including fuel gas, HVAC, fire protection, compressed air, cooling water, raw water intake, demineralization, wastewater treatment, and industrial gas systems that keep the plant and downstream compute campus online. 
  • Build, mentor, and manage a team of automation and controls engineers and technicians; scale the team with power generation capacity growth and AI supercomputer demand. 
  • Review and approve control philosophy documents, I/O lists, control narratives, single-line diagrams, electrical/pneumatic schematics, cause-and-effect diagrams, and control panel designs; drive standardized DCS/PLC/SCADA architecture, cybersecurity posture, documentation, and engineering practices across the Southaven facilities. 
  • Interface with internal engineering, construction, OEMs (turbine, HRSG, BOP, and electrical equipment vendors), and contractors; develop SOWs, negotiate, and manage contractor work to keep controls and electrical scope integrated and on schedule. 
  • Own field commissioning for automation, controls, and electrical systems (loop checks, functional testing, protection testing, start-up, and hand-off) and drive root-cause investigations and reliability improvements on operating assets. 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, or related engineering field. 
  • 8+ years of experience in automation and controls engineering, with direct experience on industrial power generation projects (gas turbine, combined cycle, or steam systems preferred) or large-scale critical power infrastructure. 
  • 3+ years of experience directly managing or leading a team of engineers (and preferably technicians). 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES: 

  • Hands-on experience with DCS, PLC, HMI, and SCADA platforms used in power generation or heavy industry (e.g., Emerson, ABB, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, SEL, Ignition), including IEC 61131 programming, industrial networking (IT/OT), and protocols such as Modbus and DNP3. 
  • Direct experience with gas turbine or combined-cycle plant controls (turbine control systems, HRSG controls, plant-wide DCS integration, and BOP), plus water treatment, wastewater, fuel gas, or process cooling systems supporting generation. 
  • Working knowledge of utility-scale and low-voltage electrical power systems, switchgear, protection, metering, and their interface with automation and controls. 
  • Experience designing or reviewing industrial control panels and electrical schematics (NFPA 79 / UL 508A; EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical, or similar) across the full project lifecycle: design, procurement, construction support, commissioning, and operations. 
  • Experience managing EPC and OEM interfaces on multi-discipline power or capital projects, and scaling a controls engineering function in a fast-growing organization. 
  • PE license in Electrical or Controls Engineering (or willingness to pursue); familiarity with ICS cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NERC CIP); experience supporting high-availability generation for critical or data center loads. 
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to remain deeply technical while mentoring engineers. 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

  • Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights, while remaining focused in hazardous environments and wearing appropriate PPE; ability to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted. 
  • Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed, and to provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies, to support power generation and critical compute operations. 
  • Must be able to work on-site at the Southaven power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceX sites. 

 

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Manager, Spaceport Events
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The hospitality team serves all employees, customers, government partners, potential clients and/or visitors with everything from meals to full-service events to corporate retreats. The Manager, Spaceport Events is a leadership role responsible for, but not limited to, staff supervision, oversight of guest services & customer satisfaction, and quality control in one or more of our event spaces. This individual works directly within hospitality leadership to properly delegate tasks, monitor the flow of service patterns, improve customer service interactions, and is the key point of contact with customers. They are also responsible for overseeing the event area upkeep and directly addressing concerns or complaints from the customers in person. The manager is able to work all service outlets and has the ability to troubleshoot equipment issues, problem solve, and communicate at a high level. They also support the mission by upholding friendly, welcoming service environments that enhance the productivity and morale of the workforce while ensuring the staff is performing to departmental and company standards. 

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Hire and manage the performance of employees on the Spaceport Events team
  • Set and enforce standards for all event operations by developing and executing detailed service plans, timelines, and schedules
  • Manage the JIRA ticketing system for all hospitality requests, including events, catering, meetings, and tours
  • Oversee the catering report for all food venues, meeting spaces, and event areas
  • Coordinate and delegate information regarding large group travel, including accommodations, transportation, and on-site activities 
  • Collaborate with fellow Hospitality leadership to plan services in shared spaces, potentially integrating traditional services
  • Ensure staff adherence to proper food safety practices
  • Create and maintain in-person and online training materials to support the training of all Hospitality roles and responsibilities
  • Monitor staff rotations, break coverage, and day-to-day responsibilities 
  • Communicate directly with vendors for order placements and to address any issues with deliveries or product quality

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High School diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 5+ years of experience in hospitality
  • 2+ years of management experience

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 3+ years hospitality management, event planning or related field
  • 5+ years of management experience
  • 7+ years of food services experience
  • Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Excellent understanding of food safety and sanitation practices
  • Advanced computer skills
  • Strong knowledge of different styles of service including counter, casual, upscale, and fine

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to carry large heavy items unassisted (up to 25lbs)
  • Ability to work gracefully under pressure
  • Able to perform frequent bending, stooping, and lifting of objects
  • Able to stand for long periods of time – up to 10 hours a day
  • Must be able to work all shifts and available for overtime, weekends and holiday as needed
  • Ability to travel and support all SpaceXAI sites as needed
  • Must participate in internal leadership and development training
  • Adaptability, problem-solving skills, and extreme attention to detail
  • Team player with the ability to collaborate effectively
  • Valid California Food Handler and RBS Certification or willingness to obtain them before employment
  • Must have or be able to obtain manager level food safety certification

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$130,000 - $160,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Material Handler is a support role for our large-scale data center construction project in Southaven, Mississippi. You will ensure construction, engineering, and trades teams have the materials they need every day. This position involves working directly in the field with planners, superintendents, technicians, and contractors to receive, stage, and deliver materials arriving at the site.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Interface with construction, engineering, and trades teams to identify and eliminate material bottlenecks in the field
  • Maintain clean, organized, and safe delivery and staging areas
  • Receive, pick up, and deliver materials to multiple work areas across the data center campus and surrounding sites
  • Stage and transport materials for daily work packages and project milestones
  • Operate material handling equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks, telehandlers, etc.) and maintain required operator qualifications
  • Build and maintain staging/delivery locations as needed, including assembling shelving, posting signage, reorganizing inventory, relocating materials, and properly disposing of trash, packaging, and scrap
  • Expedite critical materials to meet construction schedules and completion dates
  • Use inventory and scheduling systems to manage, prioritize, and fulfill material requests from work packages
  • Track and manage incoming deliveries and outgoing materials to ensure on-time availability at the point of use 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • Experience operating a forklift and/or other material-handling motorized vehicles/equipment
  • 2+ years of experience in a construction, warehousing, manufacturing, or logistics environment  

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience reading and understanding bills of materials, packing lists, or construction drawings
  • Strong communication skills for coordinating with site teams, vendors, and drivers
  • Ability to work effectively in a team as well as independently with minimal supervision
  • Ability to rapidly shift priorities in a high-paced, high-volume construction environment
  • Experience on large-scale construction, data center, warehouse, or industrial building projects
  • Mechanical aptitude or prior experience as a technician or equipment operator
  • Proficiency with computers, spreadsheets, and inventory/warehouse management software
  • Experience handling work orders, material requests, or RFIs in a construction or logistics setting

 

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Mechanical Commissioning Lead - Memphis
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking an experienced Mechanical Commissioning Lead to lead the buildout, startup, and handover of mechanical systems for SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. In this senior hands-on leadership role, you will direct commissioning, testing, troubleshooting, and turnover of critical cooling, air handling, and fluid distribution systems that support next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will lead a team of commissioning technicians while working closely with construction, engineering, operations, EPC contractors, and OEM vendors to deliver safe, reliable, and high-quality mechanical systems. This is a full-time, onsite role with extensive travel to SpaceXAI data center construction sites across the United States.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead and execute all mechanical commissioning activities for HVAC systems, chillers, cooling towers, CRAC/CRAH units, pumps, heat exchangers, piping systems, hydronic loops, and associated controls in hyperscale data center environments.
  • Direct functional performance testing, airflow/water flow verification, system balancing, integrated system testing, and system turnover to operations.
  • Oversee troubleshooting and resolution of complex mechanical, controls, and process issues during pre-commissioning, commissioning, and startup phases.
  • Develop, review, and approve detailed commissioning test procedures, scripts, checklists, and documentation in alignment with project specifications, industry standards, and SpaceXAI requirements.
  • Lead coordination with EPC contractors, OEM vendors, design engineers, and SpaceXAI stakeholders for system energization, startup sequences, and integrated system validation.
  • Mentor, supervise, and provide technical direction to Mechanical Commissioning Technicians and other field personnel; conduct performance feedback and support their development.
  • Champion safety by enforcing strict adherence to LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols; lead daily safety briefings and job hazard analyses.
  • Maintain comprehensive as-built documentation, test records, issue logs, and final commissioning reports; present readiness reports to senior leadership.
  • Support and deliver training programs for operations and maintenance teams on commissioned systems.
  • Participate in constructability reviews, design feedback sessions, and lessons-learned meetings to continuously improve installation quality and future project execution.
  • Manage commissioning schedules, resources, and punch-list resolution to meet aggressive project timelines.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 7+ years of progressive hands-on mechanical commissioning experience in data centers, power plants, semiconductor facilities, or other mission-critical industrial environments, with at least 3 years in a lead or supervisory capacity.
  • Deep expertise in data center cooling systems including large-scale chillers, cooling towers, CRAC/CRAH units, precision air handling, chilled water plants, and high-density liquid cooling technologies.
  • Strong working knowledge of commissioning test equipment (manometers, anemometers, ultrasonic flow meters, pressure/temperature calibrators, power analyzers, etc.).
  • Thorough familiarity with relevant codes and standards (ASHRAE, SMACNA, NFPA, ASME, IMC, LEED, Uptime Institute).
  • Proven ability to read, interpret, and redline mechanical drawings, P&IDs, control schematics, and sequence of operations.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience coordinating multi-discipline teams and managing contractors/vendors in fast-paced construction environments.
  • Current OSHA 30 certification (or equivalent) and strong safety leadership track record.
  • Willingness to travel extensively and work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical commissioning and startup windows.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Prior leadership on multiple hyperscale data center or mission-critical commissioning projects (100+ MW scale preferred).
  • NEBB, AABC, or equivalent Certification in Testing, Adjusting, and Balancing (TAB).
  • Hands-on experience with BMS/BAS controls troubleshooting and integration (BACnet, Modbus, LON, etc.).
  • Knowledge of refrigerant systems, direct liquid cooling, and advanced heat rejection technologies.
  • Proficiency with commissioning management platforms (CxPro, Procore, PlanGrid, or similar).
  • Technical degree or trade school certification in Mechanical Engineering Technology, HVAC, or a related field.
  • Experience implementing Integrated Systems Testing (IST) and Owner’s Project Requirements (OPR) verification.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite for extended periods during peak commissioning phases.
  • Physical capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders/stairs, lift moderate loads (up to 50 lbs), and wear full PPE for long durations.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to meet SpaceXAI's driver eligibility requirements.

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

This is a traveling role — you will mobilize with project teams to active construction sites, install and commission medium-voltage systems at 12.47 kV, 13.8 kV, and 34.5 kV, and move with the work as new facilities come online.

You will install e-house medium-voltage switchgear (MVSG), generator step-up transformers (GSUs), 15 kV and 35 kV cable, and duct bank; support hipot/VLF testing; and work adjacent to live campus buses. This is a construction and commissioning role: build new medium-voltage infrastructure from drawings and turn it over. It is not a facilities-maintenance or operating-plant role.

This is an hourly position with overtime. Expect 80% or more travel on a rotation, with per diem.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Travel with internal construction and electrical teams to project sites to install, terminate, and test medium-voltage systems, including e-house medium-voltage switchgear (MVSG), generator step-up transformers (GSUs), 15 kV and 35 kV cable, duct bank, and associated control wiring.
  • Pull, rack, land, and terminate 15 kV and 35 kV cable using manufacturer-approved stress cones and terminations.
  • Install medium-voltage duct bank, manholes, and raceway for 12.47 kV, 13.8 kV, and 34.5 kV circuits.
  • Support hipot/VLF and insulation-resistance testing of new medium-voltage cable and gear: prepare, isolate, ground, and stand the work with commissioning.
  • Work adjacent to live campus medium-voltage buses under switching orders, clearances, and LOTO.
  • Read and interpret medium-voltage one-lines, physical drawings, cable schedules, and termination drawings; produce as-builts and test records.
  • Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA 70E, OSHA 1910.269, and SpaceXAI safety and quality standards, including switching, clearance, LOTO, and arc-flash protocols.
  • Collaborate with contractors, engineers, and operations teams to deliver projects on time with zero incidents.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Facilities Operations Technician at SpaceXAI, you'll dive in, operating and maintaining the critical facility systems that power our supercomputing data centers. Working hands-on with MEP systems, you’ll tackle maintenance, operations, and repairs, ensuring peak performance and reliability. Expect to troubleshoot complex issues, streamline processes, and collaborate with teams to keep our infrastructure running smoothly, directly supporting SpaceXAI's mission to accelerate human scientific discovery through AI. 

This role includes the following positions, each with increasing responsibility:

  • Facilities Operations Technician: Independently operate and maintain critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in supercomputing data centers, ensuring high reliability and performance through hands-on maintenance, troubleshooting, and process optimization.

  • Sr Facilities Operations Technician: Perform advanced maintenance and troubleshooting of critical data center systems like HVAC, power, and environmental controls, while mentoring junior technicians to ensure operational reliability.

  • Facilities Operations Lead: Oversee the maintenance and optimization of critical data center infrastructure, including power, cooling, and environmental systems, while leading a team of technicians to ensure operational reliability and efficiency.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Responsible for MEP Infrastructure site safety and environmental compliance, ensuring the sites align with all local and regional health and safety requirements.
  • Provide operational expertise for Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) systems at the datacenter facility. The systems and equipment can include pumps, piping, chillers, cooling towers, CRAH units, wiring, lighting systems, generators, motors, water supply, UPS and switchgear, etc.
  • Routinely inspect all areas to ensure performance measures are being maintained and proactively self-report the problems of facilities.
  • Experience with writing and executing MOPs, SOPs, EOPs.
  • Perform daily inspections of critical systems.
  • Identify and maintain spare parts inventory to minimize downtime.
  • Coordinate and supervise scheduled system shutdowns.
  • Develop and implement energy monitoring metrics.
  • Support commissioning efforts by witnessing equipment startup, assisting with functional testing, and monitoring construction progress.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical or Electrical or 2+ years of hands-on operations/facilities work experience in lieu of degree (data center experience preferred).
  • Knowledge of mechanical or electrical engineering principles and systems (both would be a huge plus).
  • Experience and knowledge of all critical systems documentation including Plans, Procedures, and Operations Manuals.
  • Experience and knowledge of Building and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems and Operations.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience with PLC-based control systems and/or with Building Management Systems (Client).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and technical writing skills in English.
  • Physical Requirements:
    • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
    • Ability to utilize hand tools and power tools as needed.
    • Work is often performed in tight quarters, and physical dexterity is necessary to perform job functions.
    • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs. unassisted.
    • Comfortable working at elevated heights (up to 100 feet) with appropriate safety gear.
    • Comfortable working in extreme outdoor environments—heat, cold, rain, etc.
    • Comfortable working in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.
  • Available to work flexible shifts providing 24x7 coverage as needed, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Position is subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing.
  • Position is subject to pre-employment and annual post-employment background checks.
  • Willing to travel as needed (up to 10%).
  • Valid driver’s license.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Infrastructure Engineer to join our US Government Team, focused on designing, building, and operating secure, scalable infrastructure for critical government projects. In this role, you will develop and manage training and inference clusters, as well as highly reliable applications, across bare metal, classified cloud, and hybrid cloud architectures. You will leverage your expertise in Kubernetes and GPU hardware to deliver robust, secure systems that support large-scale AI workloads while meeting stringent federal compliance requirements. This role demands a passion for automation, observability, and ensuring system integrity in a fast-paced, high-security environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop and optimize software to provision and manage SpaceXAI's infrastructure across on-premise, virtual machine, and classified cloud environments, enabling efficient scaling for US government initiatives.
  • Enhance the reliability, performance, and cost-effectiveness of infrastructure to support large-scale AI and application workloads in secure, classified settings.
  • Collaborate with SpaceXAI engineers to understand workload requirements and design tailored solutions that meet government-specific needs and compliance standards.
  • Implement robust observability, monitoring, and security practices to ensure the integrity, availability, and confidentiality of critical systems, adhering to federal protocols.
  • Manage storage infrastructure using Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tools such as Pulumi, Terraform, or Ansible, with a focus on secure data handling.
  • Drive system reliability through incident management, postmortems, and the definition of clear SLAs and SLOs, while maintaining security and compliance.
  • This is an in-person role based in Palo Alto, CA or Washington, DC, with up to 50% travel required.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Active Top Secret (TS) security clearance.
  • 5+ years of experience as an Infrastructure Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer, or similar role, with a focus on building and maintaining reliable, scalable systems, preferably in secure or government environments.
  • Proficiency in managing storage infrastructure with IaC tools such as Pulumi, Terraform, or Ansible.
  • Deep understanding of the Kubernetes stack, including CNI, CRI, CSI, and related components.
  • Demonstrated ability to improve system reliability through incident management, postmortems, and defining SLAs/SLOs.
  • Excellent communication and documentation skills, with the ability to handle sensitive information concisely and accurately.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Deep familiarity with installing and using GPU hardware, including setting up drivers, debugging issues, and ensuring reliability.
  • Experience with high-traffic web or mobile application workloads, including optimizing Kubernetes for large-scale deployments in classified or federal settings.
  • Familiarity with chaos engineering, capacity planning, or similar practices for ensuring system resilience in government projects.
  • Proficiency with tools such as Kyverno, ArgoCD, or Go programming for infrastructure automation.
  • Strong sense of ownership, curiosity, and enthusiasm for tackling complex technical challenges in secure environments.
  • Passion for problem-solving and a proactive drive to deliver impactful results while adhering to security protocols.
  • Certifications in security-related fields (e.g., CISSP) or experience in secure federal environments.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$180,000 - $440,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.
